paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כִּלּוּ֙ לֶאֱכֹ֣ל אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֔בֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֵבִ֖יאוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם שֻׁ֖בוּ שִׁבְרוּ־לָ֥נוּ מְעַט־אֹֽכֶל׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Mitsrayim, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר אֵלָ֛יו יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הָעֵ֣ד הֵעִד֩ בָּ֨נוּ הָאִ֤ישׁ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ha'ed he'id banu ha-ish* — the paronomastic infinitive-absolute + Hiphil-finite construction of the root *ud* (Hiphil *he'id*, 'to call to witness, solemnly warn, formally attest'). The construction is a charged formal-warning idiom with concentrated cross-corpus reach: Exod 19:21, 23 (Sinai approach-prohibition); Deut 4:26; 8:19; 30:19; 31:28 ('I call heaven and earth to witness against you' — the covenantal-witness formula); 1 Sam 8:9 (Shemu'el's solemn warning to the elders about the king); 1 Kgs 2:42 (Shelomoh to Shim'i); 2 Kgs 17:13, 15; Neh 9:26, 29-30, 34; Jer 11:7; 42:19; Amos 3:13; Zech 3:6-7. The ASV 'did solemnly protest' preserves the formality. The infinitive-absolute intensifies the finite: 'warning he warned' / 'with solemn-attestation he attested'. Standard treatments: HALOT s.v. *ud* (Hiphil); BDB pp. 729-730; TDOT X:495-515; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 297; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 121; Alter *The Five Books of Moses* 2004 p. 246.

paragraphs.text: אִם־יֶשְׁךָ֛ מְשַׁלֵּ֥חַ אֶת־אָחִ֖ינוּ אִתָּ֑נוּ נֵרְדָ֕ה וְנִשְׁבְּרָ֥ה לְךָ֖ אֹֽכֶל׃

i18n.en: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:

paragraphs.text: וְאִם־אֵינְךָ֥ מְשַׁלֵּ֖חַ לֹ֣א נֵרֵ֑ד כִּֽי־הָאִ֞ישׁ אָמַ֤ר אֵלֵ֙ינוּ֙ לֹֽא־תִרְא֣וּ פָנַ֔י בִּלְתִּ֖י אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אִתְּכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: but if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down; for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לָמָ֥ה הֲרֵעֹתֶ֖ם לִ֑י לְהַגִּ֣יד לָאִ֔ישׁ הַע֥וֹד לָכֶ֖ם אָֽח׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el said, Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֡וּ שָׁא֣וֹל שָֽׁאַל־הָ֠אִישׁ לָ֣נוּ וּלְמֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֜נוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הַע֨וֹד אֲבִיכֶ֥ם חַי֙ הֲיֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֣ם אָ֔ח וַנַ֨גֶּד־ל֔וֹ עַל־פִּ֖י הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה הֲיָד֣וֹעַ נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֣י יֹאמַ֔ר הוֹרִ֖ידוּ אֶת־אֲחִיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And they said, The man asked straitly concerning ourselves, and concerning our kindred, saying, Is your father yet alive? have ye another brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we in any wise know that he would say, Bring your brother down?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוּדָ֜ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אָבִ֗יו שִׁלְחָ֥ה הַנַּ֛עַר אִתִּ֖י וְנָק֣וּמָה וְנֵלֵ֑כָה וְנִֽחְיֶה֙ וְלֹ֣א נָמ֔וּת גַּם־אֲנַ֥חְנוּ גַם־אַתָּ֖ה גַּם־טַפֵּֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: And Yehudah said unto Yisra'el his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, and also our little ones.

paragraphs.commentary: *Ha-na'ar* of Binyamin. The overlay entry `naar-lad-youth-or-attendant` was anchored at Gen 37:2 to document the chapter-specific syntactic ambiguity of the *ve-hu na'ar et-benei* clause (Yosef-as-youth vs Yosef-as-attendant-to-the-handmaid-sons); the Gen 43:8 application is to Binyamin in his early-twenties per the corpus's chronology. The Editor extends the appliesTo to GEN-WOH-43:8 as a scope-formalization: the lemma *na'ar* in the Yehudah-speech of v 8 is the same lexeme, deployed here in the affective 'young-one' register (the Rachel-line beloved-late-born) rather than the Gen 37 syntactic-crux. The entry's rationale documents that the lexeme covers the wide age-range (infant to young-man) and is not strictly age-determined.

paragraphs.text: אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֶֽעֶרְבֶ֔נּוּ מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נּוּ אִם־לֹ֨א הֲבִיאֹתִ֤יו אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וְהִצַּגְתִּ֣יו לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְחָטָ֥אתִֽי לְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:

paragraphs.commentary: *Anokhi e'ervennu mi-yadi tevaqshennu* — Yehudah's surety-pledge. The verb *arav* (here Qal imperfect 1cs + 3ms suffix, *e'ervennu*, 'I will be surety for him') and the cognate noun *eravon* ('pledge / surety') are the same root as the Gen 38 pledge-triad that Tamar extracted from Yehudah (overlay entry `eravon-pledge-triad-signet-cord-staff`, governing the *chotam*/*petil*/*matteh* set of vv 17-18, 25). The literary echo is one of the corpus's most concentrated character-arc moments: Yehudah, who once received the *eravon* (the signet, cord, and staff that Tamar later used to convict him by *haker-na*), now offers *himself* as the *arav* (the surety-person). The pledge-taker becomes the pledge-offerer; the man who once gave a pledge as a payment for a transaction now stands as the pledge for his brother's life. The literary fulcrum is widely noted: Alter *The Art of Biblical Narrative* 1981 ch. 1; Sternberg *The Poetics of Biblical Narrative* 1985 pp. 285-308; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 298; Fokkelman *Narrative Art in Genesis* SSN 17, 1975. The self-imprecatory closing *ve-chatati lekha kol ha-yamim* ('let me bear the blame for ever' ASV; literally 'and I shall be sinful before thee all the days') is the rare deployment of *chatat* in a Qal-perfect-consecutive self-curse register; the ASV-baseline rendering preserves the legal-forensic 'bear the blame' force without surfacing the *chatat* lexeme. The Gen 44:32 Yehudah-speech repetition extends the surety-pledge into the full speech-act that brings the recognition-scene of Gen 45:1 (governed by the new overlay entry with bidirectional cross-reference to the Gen 38 *eravon* triad).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֖י לוּלֵ֣א הִתְמַהְמָ֑הְנוּ כִּֽי־עַתָּ֥ה שַׁ֖בְנוּ זֶ֥ה פַעֲמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: for except we had lingered, surely we had now returned a second time.

paragraphs.commentary: *Lulei hitmahmahnu* — the Hithpalpel of the root *m-h-h* ('to tarry, delay, hesitate'), a striking reduplicated stem with a small but pointed cross-corpus distribution: Gen 19:16 (the messengers and Lot at Sedom — *va-yitmahmah*, the canonical narrative-tarrying scene); Judg 3:26 (Ehud's escape); 2 Sam 15:28 (David's *hitmahmehu*); Isa 29:9 (the prophets); Hab 2:3 (the famous *im yitmahmah chakeh lo* — the eschatological 'though it tarry, wait for it'); Ps 119:60. The ASV 'except we had lingered' preserves the counterfactual *lulei* + the Hithpalpel's tarrying-force. HALOT s.v. *mahmah*; BDB p. 554.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל אֲבִיהֶ֗ם אִם־כֵּ֣ן ׀ אֵפוֹא֮ זֹ֣את עֲשׂוּ֒ קְח֞וּ מִזִּמְרַ֤ת הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ בִּכְלֵיכֶ֔ם וְהוֹרִ֥ידוּ לָאִ֖ישׁ מִנְחָ֑ה מְעַ֤ט צֳרִי֙ וּמְעַ֣ט דְּבַ֔שׁ נְכֹ֣את וָלֹ֔ט בָּטְנִ֖ים וּשְׁקֵדִֽים׃

i18n.en: And their father Yisra'el said unto them, If it be so now, do this: take of the choice fruits of the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spicery and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:

paragraphs.commentary: Three lexical clusters converge in Ya'aqov's gift-instructions. (i) *Zimrat ha-aretz* — 'the choice produce / praise-fruits of the land'. HALOT distinguishes *zimrah* II ('strength, praise, choice produce') from the unrelated *zamar* I ('to sing'); the 'choice produce' sense at Gen 43:11 is a near-hapax (the homophonous Exod 15:2 *ozzi ve-zimrat Yah* is contested between 'song / praise' and 'strength / might' readings and belongs to the separate *zimrah* I lexeme). ASV-baseline 'choice fruits of the land' retained. (ii) The four-item aromatics-list *me'at tzori u-me'at devash, nekhot va-lot, botnim u-shqedim* — *tzeri*, *nekhot*, and *lot* are governed by the existing overlay `nekhot-tzeri-lot-caravan-spices` (the Yishme'elite caravan's Gen 37:25 cargo) whose appliesTo is now extended to GEN-WOH-43:11; the four additional lexemes are *devash* ('honey / date-syrup'; the 'land flowing with milk and honey' formula recurs from Exod 3:8), *botnim* ('pistachio nuts' — *Pistacia vera* — chapter-singular hapax in the HB, a Levantine luxury-item), and *shqedim* ('almonds' — cross-corpus reach at Num 17:23 [MT 17:8] Aharon's budding rod, Eccl 12:5 the almond-tree blossoming, and Jer 1:11 *maqqel shaqed* the prophetic almond-rod with the *shaqed*/*shoqed* watchful-word pun). ASV-baseline 'a little balm, and a little honey, spicery and myrrh, nuts, and almonds' retained. (iii) *Kelim* in *bi-kheleikhem* extends the existing overlay `kelim-sak-amtachat-sack-vocabulary-alternation-gen42-44` (the chapter's broader sack-and-vessel vocabulary). HALOT s.vv. *zimrah*, *devash*, *boten*, *shaqed*; Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 298; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 p. 122.

paragraphs.text: וְכֶ֥סֶף מִשְׁנֶ֖ה קְח֣וּ בְיֶדְכֶ֑ם וְאֶת־הַכֶּ֜סֶף הַמּוּשָׁ֨ב בְּפִ֤י אַמְתְּחֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ תָּשִׁ֣יבוּ בְיֶדְכֶ֔ם אוּלַ֥י מִשְׁגֶּ֖ה הֽוּא׃

i18n.en: and take double money in your hand; and the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks carry again in your hand; peradventure it was an oversight:

paragraphs.commentary: Two lexical decisions. (i) *Mishneh kesef* — 'double money'. The noun *mishneh* spans the corpus in two registers: the simple-doubling commercial sense (here at Gen 43:12, 15; Exod 16:5, 22 the double-portion of Sabbath manna; Deut 15:18) and the ordinal/office-title sense ('second' — Gen 41:43 *mirkevet ha-mishneh* the chariot-of-the-second; Deut 17:18 *mishneh ha-torah*; 1 Sam 23:17; 2 Kgs 22:14 = 2 Chr 34:22 Hulda's *mishneh* / second-quarter). The Gen 41:43 office-title sense is governed by the overlay `mirkevet-ha-mishneh-chariot-of-the-second-gen41`; the Gen 43:12 commercial-doubling sense is registered in the new overlay entry with cross-reference to the Gen 41 sibling. (ii) *Mishgeh* — 'oversight / inadvertence'. The noun is chapter-singular in the HB; its verbal root *shagah* / *shagag* ('to err inadvertently') is the standard Levitical inadvertent-sin lexeme (Lev 4:2, 13, 22, 27; 5:15, 18; Num 15:22-29). ASV-baseline 'peradventure it was an oversight' retained. HALOT s.vv. *mishneh*, *mishgeh*.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֖ם קָ֑חוּ וְק֖וּמוּ שׁ֥וּבוּ אֶל־הָאִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֣ל שַׁדַּ֗י יִתֵּ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם רַחֲמִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָאִ֔ישׁ וְשִׁלַּ֥ח לָכֶ֛ם אֶת־אֲחִיכֶ֥ם אַחֵ֖ר וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ין וַאֲנִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁכֹ֖לְתִּי שָׁכָֽלְתִּי׃

i18n.en: and El Shaddai give you mercy before the man, that he may release unto you your other brother and Binyamin. And as for me, if I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.

paragraphs.commentary: Three lexical-theological items converge in Ya'aqov's send-off. (i) *El Shaddai* — Ya'aqov's invocation of the West-Semitic high-god compound; the central entry `el-shaddai` governs the patriarchal-narrative occurrences (Gen 17:1, 28:3, 35:11, 43:14, 48:3, 49:25), all in P or P-adjacent material per Friedman, with the three modern etymologies (*shadad* / Akkadian *šadû* 'mountain' / West-Semitic class-epithet *Šaddai* attested at Deir 'Alla) documented; appliesTo normalized to GEN-WOH-43:14. (ii) *Rachamim* — the new central entry `rachamim-compassion-womb-root` governs the lexeme's foundational cross-corpus distribution (the noun derived from the *rechem* 'womb' root, naming divine and human compassion across Exod 34:6 the gracious-and-compassionate formula, Deut 13:18, Isa 47:6 + 54:7 + 63:7 + 63:15, Hos 2:21, the Psalter, Daniel, Nehemiah, Chronicles). (iii) *Ka'asher shakholti shakhalti* — Ya'aqov's resignation-formula, the double Qal-perfect-1cs construction matching Esther 4:16 *ka'asher avadti avadti* ('if I perish, I perish'); the central entry `shakhol-bereavement-of-children-vocabulary` (anchored Gen 42:36) has appliesTo extended to GEN-WOH-43:14 and the Esther 4:16 cross-corpus echo is noted in its rationale. ASV-baseline 'El Shaddai give you mercy before the man ... if I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved' retained.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְח֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וּמִשְׁנֶה־כֶּ֛סֶף לָקְח֥וּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְאֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֑ן וַיָּקֻ֙מוּ֙ וַיֵּרְד֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יוֹסֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Binyamin; and rose up, and went down to Mitsrayim, and stood before Yosef.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨רְא יוֹסֵ֣ף אִתָּם֮ אֶת־בִּנְיָמִין֒ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לַֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ הָבֵ֥א אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים הַבָּ֑יְתָה וּטְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֙בַח֙ וְהָכֵ֔ן כִּ֥י אִתִּ֛י יֹאכְל֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בַּֽצָּהֳרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And when Yosef saw Binyamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, Bring the men into the house, and slay, and make ready; for the men shall dine with me at noon.

paragraphs.commentary: *La-asher al beito* — 'to him who is over his house', the standard idiom for the chief-of-household / steward / household-administrator. The idiom recurs across the cycle (Gen 43:19; 44:1, 4 — the same steward) and is the technical-administrative title of a recognized ANE household-office; cross-corpus distribution into royal-administration vocabulary (the *asher al ha-bayit* as chief minister: 1 Kgs 4:6; 16:9; 18:3; 2 Kgs 10:5; 15:5; 18:18, 37; 19:2 = Isa 36:3, 22; 37:2; Isa 22:15 — the Shevna / Elyaqim succession that is the corpus's most concentrated treatment of the office). The new overlay entry documents the office and the load-bearing recurrence in the Gen 43-44 stewardship-scenes; a future Kings/Isaiah translation may justify central promotion. The paronomastic *u-tevoach tevach* ('slay a slaying') deploys the verb *tabach* and the cognate noun *tevach* — the same root as the central `sar-ha-tabbachim-captain-of-the-guard` (Potifar's office at Gen 37:36; 39:1), a lexical echo whereby Yosef commanding the slaughter-for-feast recapitulates the *tabbachim* role he once stood under.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הָאִ֔ישׁ כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֥יתָה יוֹסֵֽף׃

i18n.en: And the man did as Yosef bade; and the man brought the men to Yosef's house.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּ֣י הֽוּבְאוּ֮ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵף֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ עַל־דְּבַ֤ר הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ הַשָּׁ֤ב בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵ֙ינוּ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה אֲנַ֖חְנוּ מֽוּבָאִ֑ים לְהִתְגֹּלֵ֤ל עָלֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּלְהִתְנַפֵּ֣ל עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְלָקַ֧חַת אֹתָ֛נוּ לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְאֶת־חֲמֹרֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: And the men were afraid, because they were brought to Yosef's house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses.

paragraphs.commentary: *Le-hitgolel aleinu u-le-hitnafel aleinu* — 'to roll [himself] upon us and to fall [himself] upon us'. The Hithpael of *galal* ('roll') paired with the Hithpael of *naphal* ('fall') is a chapter-singular violence-idiom in the HB. *Hitgolel* — the 'roll oneself against / seek pretext / fall upon' sense — is rare (2 Sam 20:12 has *mitgolel ba-dam* of Amasa's body; the aggressive 'seek occasion' sense is here). *Hitnafel* — the 'fall upon (in attack)' sense — is rare (the cognate Hithpael more often names the supplicatory prostration of Deut 9:18, 25 or Ezra 10:1). The two Hithpaels in series at Gen 43:18 are unique; ASV-baseline 'that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us' preserves the violence-and-pretext register. HALOT s.vv. *galal* (Hithpael), *naphal* (Hithpael); Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 299.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ אֶל־הָאִ֔ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו פֶּ֥תַח הַבָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: And they came near to the steward of Yosef's house, and they spake unto him at the door of the house,

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֑י יָרֹ֥ד יָרַ֛דְנוּ בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לִשְׁבָּר־אֹֽכֶל׃

i18n.en: and said, Oh, my lord, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food:

paragraphs.text: וַֽיְהִ֞י כִּי־בָ֣אנוּ אֶל־הַמָּל֗וֹן וַֽנִּפְתְּחָה֙ אֶת־אַמְתְּחֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֤ה כֶֽסֶף־אִישׁ֙ בְּפִ֣י אַמְתַּחְתּ֔וֹ כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּמִשְׁקָל֑וֹ וַנָּ֥שֶׁב אֹת֖וֹ בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: and it came to pass, when we came to the lodging-place, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.

paragraphs.commentary: The brothers' diplomatic retelling of the Gen 42:27-28 *malon*-discovery scene. The original narration foregrounded the *einennu*-shock of the brothers' discovery (*va-yetze libbam* — 'their heart went out'); the brothers' present-tense retelling compresses the shock into the matter-of-fact 'every man's money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight'. The overlay entries `malon-lodging-place-wayfaring-stopover-gen42` and `kelim-sak-amtachat-sack-vocabulary-alternation-gen42-44` have their appliesTo extended to cover the chapter's recurrences (a scope-formalization, no decision change).

paragraphs.text: וְכֶ֧סֶף אַחֵ֛ר הוֹרַ֥דְנוּ בְיָדֵ֖נוּ לִשְׁבָּר־אֹ֑כֶל לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְנוּ מִי־שָׂ֥ם כַּסְפֵּ֖נוּ בְּאַמְתְּחֹתֵֽינוּ׃

i18n.en: And other money have we brought down in our hand to buy food: we know not who put our money in our sacks.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ שָׁל֨וֹם לָכֶ֜ם אַל־תִּירָ֗אוּ אֱלֹ֨הֵיכֶ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י אֲבִיכֶם֙ נָתַ֨ן לָכֶ֤ם מַטְמוֹן֙ בְּאַמְתְּחֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם כַּסְפְּכֶ֖ם בָּ֣א אֵלָ֑י וַיּוֹצֵ֥א אֲלֵהֶ֖ם אֶת־שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And he said, Peace be to you, fear not: your Elohim, and the Elohim of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: your money came to me. And he brought Shim'on out unto them.

paragraphs.commentary: Two items. (i) The steward's twofold appeal to *Elohekhem ve-Elohei avikhem* ('your Elohim, and the Elohim of your father') — the third Elohim-on-character's-lips occurrence in close sequence (Yosef at Gen 42:18, brothers at Gen 42:28, steward here), confirming the cycle's sustained Elohim-default. The cycle's narrator-voice remains Elohim-only outside the Gen 39 YHWH-frame; the appliesTo of `yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim` extends to GEN-WOH-43:23 and GEN-WOH-43:29. Whether the steward is a Yosef-informed character (so the rabbinic reading: an insider) or simply diplomatic (mirroring the brothers' own framing) is undecidable from the text. (ii) *Matmon* — 'treasure / hidden store', from *taman* 'to bury / hide'. The new overlay entry documents the lexeme's cross-corpus reach: Isa 45:3 *matmonei mistarim* ('treasures of secret places' — the famous Cyrus-prophecy); Jer 41:8 (*matmonim* hidden in the field); Job 3:21 (*ke-tomenim li-matmonim*); Prov 2:4. ASV-baseline 'treasure' retained.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֥א הָאִ֛ישׁ אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים בֵּ֣יתָה יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּתֶּן־מַ֙יִם֙ וַיִּרְחֲצ֣וּ רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּתֵּ֥ן מִסְפּ֖וֹא לַחֲמֹֽרֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And the man brought the men into Yosef's house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּכִ֙ינוּ֙ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֔ה עַד־בּ֥וֹא יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י שָֽׁמְע֔וּ כִּי־שָׁ֖ם יֹ֥אכְלוּ לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: And they made ready the present against Yosef's coming at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיָּבִ֥יאּוּ ל֛וֹ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָדָ֖ם הַבָּ֑יְתָה וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֖וֹ אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And when Yosef came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed down to him to the earth.

paragraphs.commentary: **Second *hishtachavah*-fulfilment of Yosef's Gen 37:7 sheaves-dream.** The brothers, bringing the *minchah* and prostrating *artzah* ('to the earth'), repeat the Gen 42:6 first fulfilment under intensified conditions: this time Binyamin is with them (so the eleven-sheaf scene of Gen 37:7 is being approached), and the *minchah* (the Gen 32 / 33 Esav-appeasement vocabulary now redeployed) makes the lordship-acknowledgement structurally explicit. The central entry `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` (promoted from the overlay at the Gen 42:6 first-fulfilment) has its appliesTo extended to cover GEN-WOH-43:26 and (with the v 28 *qadad*+*hishtachavah* pair) GEN-WOH-43:28. The *minchah* lexeme's appliesTo also extends from the Gen 32 Esav-appeasement anchor to cover the chapter's gift-and-prostration recurrences (Gen 43:11, 15, 25, 26): the same lexeme used of Ya'aqov's appeasement-of-Esav is now used of the brothers' approach to the disguised Yosef. ASV-baseline 'bowed down to him to the earth' retained at this verse (the central entry's standard 'made obeisance' is preserved as the consistency-rendering across the cycle but the *artzah* intensifier admits the ASV's local-variation; the literary point is the prostration-itself, not the rendering).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל לָהֶם֙ לְשָׁל֔וֹם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲשָׁל֛וֹם אֲבִיכֶ֥ם הַזָּקֵ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֑ם הַעוֹדֶ֖נּוּ חָֽי׃

i18n.en: And he asked them of their welfare, and said, Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ שָׁל֛וֹם לְעַבְדְּךָ֥ לְאָבִ֖ינוּ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ חָ֑י וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וישתחו [וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ׃]

i18n.en: And they said, Thy servant our father is well, he is yet alive. And they bowed the head, and made obeisance.

paragraphs.commentary: **Second hishtachavah-occurrence in the chapter, paired with *qadad* (Qal *va-yiqqedu*, 'and they bowed the head').** The *qadad* + *hishtachavah* pairing is a fixed formal-obeisance formula across the corpus: Gen 24:26 (Avraham's servant — *va-yiqqod va-yishtachu*); Gen 24:48 (the servant's retelling); Exod 4:31 (the elders before Mosheh and Aharon); Exod 12:27 (the people at the Pesach instruction); Exod 34:8 (Mosheh at the theophany); Num 22:31 (Bil'am before the messenger); 1 Sam 24:8 [MT 24:9]; 28:14; 1 Kgs 1:16, 31; 2 Chr 20:18; 29:30; Neh 8:6. The new central entry `qadad-bow-the-head-paired-prostration-formula` governs the lexeme and its paired-formula function; the central `hishtachavah-bow-down-obeisance-worship` appliesTo is extended to GEN-WOH-43:28. The ketiv *vishtachu* (וישתחו) is rendered by the qere as *va-yishtachavu* (וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲוּוּ — fully-vocalized Hishtaphel); the standard qere is uncontested. ASV-baseline 'they bowed the head, and made obeisance' preserves both verbs.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־בִּנְיָמִ֣ין אָחִיו֮ בֶּן־אִמּוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲזֶה֙ אֲחִיכֶ֣ם הַקָּטֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּ֖ם אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים יָחְנְךָ֖ בְּנִֽי׃

i18n.en: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw Binyamin his brother, his mother's son, and said, Is this your youngest brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, Elohim be gracious unto thee, my son.

paragraphs.commentary: Two items. (i) *Ben-immo* — 'his mother's son' — the marked literary phrasing that names Binyamin specifically as Rachel's son, the only one of the eleven brothers present who shares Yosef's mother. The phrasing is rare in the patriarchal narratives (cf. Deut 13:7 [MT 13:6] *achikha ben-immekha*; Judg 8:19 of Gid'on's slain brothers *bnei immi*; Ps 50:20; 69:9 [MT 69:8] *muzar hayiti le-echai ve-nakhri li-vnei immi*). The phrasing is a literary marker of the Rachel-line bond and is observed across mainstream commentary (Sarna, Westermann, Alter). Commentary-only observation; no glossary entry. (ii) *Elohim yochanekha beni* — 'Elohim be gracious unto thee, my son'. The verb *chanan* ('be gracious') in the imperfect-3ms jussive form with the 2ms suffix is the standard grace-and-favor verb; the verbal form *yochanekha* directly echoes the Aaronic blessing of Num 6:25 (*ya'er YHWH panav eilekha vichunekka* — the same Qal-jussive of *chanan*, 3ms + 2ms). Yosef's use of *Elohim* (not YHWH) extends the cycle's Elohim-on-character's-lips pattern; the overlay `yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim` appliesTo extends to GEN-WOH-43:29.

paragraphs.text: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר יוֹסֵ֗ף כִּֽי־נִכְמְר֤וּ רַחֲמָיו֙ אֶל־אָחִ֔יו וַיְבַקֵּ֖שׁ לִבְכּ֑וֹת וַיָּבֹ֥א הַחַ֖דְרָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

i18n.en: And Yosef made haste; for his heart yearned over his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

paragraphs.commentary: *Nikhmeru rachamav el achiv* — 'his *rachamim* burned / grew warm toward his brother'. The Niphal of *kamar* I ('to be hot, grow warm, burn') paired with *rachamim* (the womb-compassion noun) generates the corpus's most concentrated compassion-yearning idiom. The cross-corpus parallels are decisive: **1 Kgs 3:26** — the famous Solomon-judgment scene, the true mother's *nikhmeru rachameha al benah* ('her *rachamim* burned for her son') — verbatim the same Niphal+*rachamim* construction; **Hos 11:8** — *nikhmeru nichumai* ('my compassions are stirred together', YHWH's lament over Ephraim). The three occurrences (Gen 43:30, 1 Kgs 3:26, Hos 11:8) form a tight cross-corpus *nikhmar*+compassion idiom-cluster, and the Genesis 43 occurrence is the corpus's first. The new overlay entry `nikhmeru-rachamav-compassion-burning-idiom-gen43` documents the idiom with bidirectional cross-reference to the new central entry `rachamim-compassion-womb-root` (the parent lexeme). ASV-baseline 'his heart yearned over his brother' retained — modernizing the visceral KJV 'bowels did yearn' that preserves the *rachamim* anatomical-affective force; the literal-*rachamim* alternative documented in the glossary rationale. HALOT s.vv. *kamar* I (Niphal), *rachamim*; BDB pp. 485, 933; TDOT VII:153-159 (kamar), XIII:439-450 (rachamim); Sarna *JPS Genesis* 1989 p. 301; Westermann *Genesis 37-50* 1986 pp. 124-125.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּרְחַ֥ץ פָּנָ֖יו וַיֵּצֵ֑א וַיִּ֨תְאַפַּ֔ק וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שִׂ֥ימוּ לָֽחֶם׃

i18n.en: And he washed his face, and came out; and he refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yit'appaq* — 'and he restrained / refrained / controlled himself'. The Hithpael of *afaq* is a striking and rare emotional-restraint lexeme with a load-bearing cross-corpus distribution and a structurally pivotal Yosef-cycle deployment. The Gen 43:31 occurrence is structurally paired with Gen 45:1 (*ve-lo yakhol Yosef le-hit'appeq* — 'Yosef could not refrain himself', the disclosure-scene): Yosef restrains himself here and FAILS to restrain himself at the disclosure. The Gen 43:31 → Gen 45:1 antithesis is one of the corpus's most concentrated emotional-arc markers (Alter, Sternberg, Fokkelman). Cross-corpus reach: 1 Sam 13:12 (Sha'ul *va-et'appaq* — 'I forced myself' to offer the sacrifice); Isa 42:14 (YHWH's silence: *hechesheti me-olam achrish et'appaq*); Isa 63:15; 64:11 [MT 64:12] (the divine 'will you restrain yourself?' lament); Esth 5:10 (Haman *va-yit'appaq Haman*). The new central entry `yitappaq-emotional-restraint-yosef-arc` documents the lexeme and the load-bearing Gen 43:31 → 45:1 cycle-arc. ASV-baseline 'he refrained himself' retained.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ ל֛וֹ לְבַדּ֖וֹ וְלָהֶ֣ם לְבַדָּ֑ם וְלַמִּצְרִ֞ים הָאֹכְלִ֤ים אִתּוֹ֙ לְבַדָּ֔ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יוּכְל֜וּן הַמִּצְרִ֗ים לֶאֱכֹ֤ל אֶת־הָֽעִבְרִים֙ לֶ֔חֶם כִּי־תוֹעֵבָ֥ה הִ֖וא לְמִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Mitsrim, that did eat with him, by themselves: because the Mitsrim might not eat bread with the Ivrim; for that is an abomination unto the Mitsrim.

paragraphs.commentary: **MAJOR central addition: *to'evah*.** The lexeme *to'evah* ('abomination') is one of the most load-bearing keywords in the HB, anchoring the Priestly+Holiness-Code abomination-prohibitions (Lev 18:22, 26, 27, 29, 30; 20:13), the Deuteronomic abomination-laws (Deut 7:25, 26; 12:31; 13:14; 14:3; 17:1, 4; 18:9, 12; 20:18; 22:5; 23:18 [MT 23:19]; 24:4; 25:16; 27:15; 32:16), the prophetic abomination-saturation (most concentrated in Ezekiel — 43 occurrences; also Isa, Jer, Hos, Mal), and the wisdom-keyword (Prov: 18 occurrences; Job 30:10). Gen 43:32 is the **corpus's first attested *to'evah*** and the prose-narrative Genesis anchor of this corpus-wide moral-cultic-theological keyword. The new central entry `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword` documents the cross-corpus reach, the Priestly / Deuteronomic / prophetic / wisdom register-distinctions, and the comparative-ANE context (Herodotus II.41 on Egyptian dietary taboos; Vergote and Redford on the Gen 43:32 ethnographic verisimilitude). The narrator's explanatory clause *ki to'evah hi le-Mitzrayim* is the HB's earliest documented ethnographic note on Egyptian dietary/social-segregation practice. *Ha-Ivrim* (plural gentilic) extends the central `ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology` appliesTo (normalized to GEN-WOH-43:32 to match the corpus convention). ASV-baseline 'because the Mitsrim might not eat bread with the Ivrim; for that is an abomination unto the Mitsrim' retained with WoH proper-name transliterations.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו הַבְּכֹר֙ כִּבְכֹ֣רָת֔וֹ וְהַצָּעִ֖יר כִּצְעִרָת֑וֹ וַיִּתְמְה֥וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אִ֥ישׁ אֶל־רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one with another.

paragraphs.commentary: **The impossible-knowledge seating-by-birthright literary observation.** The narrator notes that Yosef seated the brothers *ha-bekhor ki-vkhorato ve-ha-tza'ir ki-tze'irato* — 'the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth' — and that the brothers marveled (Qal *va-yitmehu*) one to another. The seating is impossible knowledge for the disguised Egyptian official; the brothers' marveling is the narrative's structural foreshadowing of the Gen 45 disclosure-scene. Standard mainstream-noted reading (Sarna, Alter, Sternberg, Fokkelman): a deliberate identity-hint placed on the surface for the attentive reader. The verb *tamah* ('to marvel / be astonished') has cross-corpus reach into Isa 13:8; 29:9; Jer 4:9; Hab 1:5; Ps 48:6 [MT 48:5]; Job 26:11; Eccl 5:7 [MT 5:8]. The new overlay entry documents the chapter-singular Genesis deployment and the literary observation.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א מַשְׂאֹ֜ת מֵאֵ֣ת פָּנָיו֮ אֲלֵהֶם֒ וַתֵּ֜רֶב מַשְׂאַ֧ת בִּנְיָמִ֛ן מִמַּשְׂאֹ֥ת כֻּלָּ֖ם חָמֵ֣שׁ יָד֑וֹת וַיִּשְׁתּ֥וּ וַֽיִּשְׁכְּר֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Binyamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.

paragraphs.commentary: Three items. (i) *Mas'ot* / *mas'at* — 'portions' (from *nasa* 'to lift up'), the stately court-meal lexeme. The construction 'lift up portions from before his face to them' is a court-ceremonial idiom; the noun *mas'eit* has broader senses elsewhere (2 Sam 11:8 King David's *mas'at*; Esth 2:18; Jer 38:14; 40:5; Ps 141:2 of the uplifted hands). The Gen 43:34 portion-of-the-feast specialization is documented in the new overlay entry. (ii) *Chamesh yadot* — 'five hands / five portions / fivefold'. The construction *yad* in the 'portion / share / part' sense is well-attested (2 Sam 19:43 [MT 19:44] *eser yadot li ba-melekh*, 'ten parts in the king'; 2 Kgs 11:7 = 2 Chr 23:8 — the *yadot* divisions of the Levitical guards); the *chamesh yadot* fivefold-portion at Gen 43:34 is the corpus's first 'X yadot' fractional-portion construction. The Gen 41:34 *chimmesh* (Piel of ch-m-sh, the administrative-fifth verb, governed by overlay `chimmesh-fifth-part-or-fifth-division-gen41`) deploys the same root in a different construction (one-fifth fraction vs. fivefold-multiplier); the new overlay entry distinguishes the two. (iii) *Va-yishtu va-yishkeru immo* — 'and they drank, and were merry with him' (ASV) / 'they drank and became drunk with him' (literal). The verb *shakhar* (Qal *va-yishkeru*) is the standard 'become drunk' verb (cf. Gen 9:21 Noah *va-yishkar* — the corpus's first drunkenness, with negative outcome); the rendering choice between 'were merry' (ASV/KJV — euphemistic) and 'became drunk' (NJPS / Alter — literal) is registered in the new overlay entry, with the Gen 9:21 echo noted as the literary cross-reference (the brothers' drinking-to-merry in the disguised-presence of the brother they once stripped echoes Noah's drinking-to-uncovered-nakedness). ASV-baseline 'were merry' retained.
